{{Short description|Formula for expressing the global error of a perturbation}}
The '''Alekseev–Gröbner formula,''' or nonlinear variation-of-constants formula, is a generalization of the linear [[variation of constants]] formula which was proven independently by [[Wolfgang Gröbner]] in 1960<ref>{{cite book |last1=Gröbner |first1=Wolfgang |title=Die Lie-Reihen und Ihre Anwendungen. |date=1960 |publisher=VEB Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften |location=Berlin}}</ref> and [[Vladimir Mikhailovich Alekseev]] in 1961.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alekseev |first1=V. |title=An estimate for the perturbations of the solution of ordinary differential equations (Russian). |journal=Vestn. Mosk. Univ., Ser. I, Math. Meh. |volume=2, 1961}}</ref> It expresses the global error of a perturbation in terms of the local error and has many applications for studying perturbations of [[Ordinary differential equation|ordinary differential equations]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Iserles |first1=A. |title=A first course in the numerical analysis of differential equations |date=2009 |publisher=Cambridge Texts in Applied Mathematics, Cambridge University Press |location=Cambridge |edition=second}}</ref>

== Formulation ==

Let <math>d \in \mathbb N</math> be a [[natural number]], let <math>T \in (0, \infty)</math> be a positive [[real number]], and let <math>\mu \colon [0, T] \times \mathbb{R}^{d} \to \mathbb{R}^{d} \in C^{0, 1}([0, T] \times \mathbb{R}^{d})</math> be a function which is continuous on the time interval <math>[0, T]</math> and continuously differentiable on the <math>d</math>-dimensional space <math>\mathbb{R}^{d}</math>. Let <math>X \colon [0, T]^{2} \times \mathbb{R}^{d} \to \mathbb{R}^{d}</math>, <math> (s, t, x) \mapsto X_{s, t}^{x}</math> be a continuous solution of the integral equation
<math display="block">X_{s, t}^{x} = x + \int_{s}^{t} \mu(r, X_{s, r}^{x}) dr.</math>
Furthermore, let <math>Y \in C^{1}([0, T], \mathbb{R}^{d})</math> be continuously differentiable. We view <math>Y</math> as the unperturbed function, and <math>X</math> as the perturbed function. Then it holds that
<math display="block">
X_{0, T}^{Y_{0}} - Y_{T} = \int_{0}^{T} \left( \frac{\partial}{\partial x} X_{r, T}^{Y_{s}} \right) \left( \mu(r, Y_{r}) - \frac{d}{dr} Y_{r} \right) dr.
</math>
The Alekseev–Gröbner formula allows to express the global error <math>X_{0, T}^{Y_{0}} - Y_{T}</math> in terms of the local error <math>( \mu(r, Y_{r}) - \tfrac{d}{dr} Y_{r}) </math>.

== The Itô–Alekseev–Gröbner formula ==

The Itô–Alekseev–Gröbner formula<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hudde |first1=A. |last2=Hutzenthaler |first2=M. |last3=Jentzen |first3=A. |last4=Mazzonetto |first4=S. |title=On the Itô–Alekseev–Gröbner formula for stochastic differential equations |journal=Annales de l'Institut Henri Poincaré, Probabilités et Statistiques |year=2024 |volume=60 |issue=2 |doi=10.1214/21-AIHP1199 |arxiv=1812.09857}}</ref> is a generalization of the Alekseev–Gröbner formula which states in the deterministic case, that for a continuously differentiable function <math>f \in C^{1}(\mathbb R^{k}, \mathbb R^{d})</math> it holds that
<math display="block">
f(X_{0, T}^{Y_{0}}) - f(Y_{T}) =
\int_{0}^{T} f'\left( \frac{\partial}{\partial x} X_{r, T}^{Y_{s}} \right) \frac{\partial}{\partial x} X_{s, T}^{Y_{s}}\left( \mu(r, Y_{r}) - \frac{d}{dr} Y_{r} \right) dr.
</math>
